correctness.rationale: All forcing sets have at most two initial whites per part; a complete four-case criterion using matched-index sets is proved in both directions. Its two-plus-two equality obstruction is counted exactly; a,b>=4 then forces domination by black-neighbor counts. The exact complement count establishes all five polynomial coefficients and positive leading terms in each t regime. An independent adjacency-based exhaustive checker reproduces every coefficient for 50 profiles and verifies a boundary counterexample.

value.rationale: For an unbounded two-parameter dense family subjected to a natural sparse operation, the theorem settles both exact parameters and the complete all-cardinality forcing polynomial. The t=1 and t>=2 phases sharply reduce the minimum, and exact multiplicities classify all optimizing initial sets. It proves the stronger all-set domination property with a genuine small-part boundary, not just an isolated small enumeration.
